gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the A229 Ultra's 4K rear camera (RNE800, and the waterproof RWE800) works only with the A229 Ultra front unit, not the A229 Pro or Plus, or that it runs over a Type-C cable VIOFO says 'cannot be extended manually by connecting other USB cables'. The box has 6 m; 8 m and 10 m cables are sold separately.
standout_why: I read the pages ChatGPT cited or ranked. ProductBible 'Best 4K Dash Cams' and 'Best Front and Rear Dash Cams', both dated 2026-11-19, list the A229 Ultra as 4K30 front and 4K30 rear. They name no processor and give no bitrate or HDR behaviour in dual mode. The front-and-rear page only says to 'check the length included' for the rear cable. VIOFO's FAQ, which ChatGPT cited, already explains the processing budget in VIOFO's own words: 'processing power is split across three cameras' (A329SW), and '4K 60fps is only available when using two cameras' and HDR 'disables 60fps' (A329S). It also says the A229 Ultra records dual 4K with HDR on both channels. So the general mechanism (one processor shared by all channels, so dual 4K runs at 30 fps) is partly covered by a cited rival. The rear-module lock-in and the cable that can't be extended are new. Car and Driver could not be fetched; viofo.com's 4K collection page returned HTTP 429.
decides: This confirms the VIOFO A229 Ultra 2CH as the pick for true dual 4K. VIOFO says both channels record 3840×2160 at the same time with HDR active on both. It also limits the plan in two ways. An A229 Pro owner cannot get dual 4K by adding a rear camera, because the 4K rear works only with the Ultra front unit, so they must buy the whole Ultra. SUV, van and truck owners must order an 8 m or 10 m cable ($9.99) instead of joining USB extensions. Vantrue's S1 Pro Max 4K+4K honestly wins the price segment of dual 4K: $239.99 on vantrue.com against $409.99 for the A229 Ultra 2CH on viofo.com, both read 2026-11-21. DashCamTalk's spec table lists it with two IMX678 sensors at 4K30 each on a Novatek NT98529. Its rear HDR is disputed: DashCamTalk's spec table says no rear HDR, while forum reviewer TonyM says 'The Rear camera supports HDR'. Vantrue's own page must settle this before the page states it. The S1 Pro Max 4K+4K has no product record yet. It belongs in the table and is in stock at $239.99 (variant 51200752189749).
